title: Remove Spaces
directAnswer: Append each non-space character to a builder and return it. Use a StringBuilder in Java to avoid O(n²) concatenation.

remember.takeaway: Build filtered strings with a builder, never repeated concatenation.
remember.formula: sb=builder; for ch: if ch!=' ': sb.append(ch)
antiSignals: Reaching for += in a loop — use a builder

problemStatement: Given a string `s`, return a copy with all space characters removed.
understanding: Build a new string from only the non-space characters.

approaches.name: Filtered build
approaches.whenToMention: This is the standard, expected solution — lead with it.
approaches.explanation:
Filter out spaces by appending only non-space characters to a builder. The key performance point: use a `StringBuilder` (Java) or `''.join` (Python), never repeated `+=` on a String.

**Why `+=` in a loop is O(n²).** Java/Python strings are immutable, so each `s += ch` allocates a brand-new string and copies all previous characters. Over n appends that's 1+2+…+n = O(n²) copying. A StringBuilder appends into a growable buffer in amortised O(1), keeping the whole build O(n).

**Remove-all vs trim.** This removes *every* space, not just leading/trailing (that's `trim`). Be sure which the prompt wants.

**Generalises to any filter.** Swap the `ch != ' '` predicate for any rule and you have a generic 'keep characters matching X' transform.

code.python:
def remove_spaces(s: str) -> str:
    return ''.join(ch for ch in s if ch != ' ')

hints: Append only the characters you want to keep.
Use a StringBuilder / join — why not `+=` in a loop?
Remove-all is different from trim (leading/trailing only).
approaches.insight: Calling out the StringBuilder-vs-`+=` performance trap is a nice senior touch.
approaches.complexityReasoning: one pass appending into a growable buffer — O(n) time with amortised O(1) appends.
pitfalls: Only trimming ends instead of removing all spaces.

commonMistakes: Only removing leading/trailing spaces (that's trim, not remove-all).

followupVariations.title: Replace a Character
followupVariations.hint: Same build, mapping instead of filtering.

patternNote: A core fresher pattern: Filtered build. Master it on small inputs and it transfers to harder problems.

commonMistakesDetailed.title: String += in a loop
commonMistakesDetailed.why: Immutable strings copy everything on each +=, making the build O(n²); a StringBuilder is O(n).
commonMistakesDetailed.bad: String r = ""; for (char ch : ...) if (ch!=' ') r += ch;   // O(n^2)
